items.title: Oriented interval meshes and broken polynomial spaces
items.statement:
Let $a<b$ and choose an integer $N\ge1$ and points
$$a=x_0<x_1<\cdots<x_N=b.$$
The **oriented interval mesh** is the ordered family of cells $I_j=(x_{j-1},x_j)$, $1\le j\le N$, each oriented from left to right. Write $h_j=x_j-x_{j-1}>0$. For an integer $p\ge0$, the **broken polynomial space** is
$$V_h^{\mathrm{br}}=\prod_{j=1}^N\mathbb P_p(I_j),$$
with functions interpreted cell by cell. At an interior node $x_j$, write $w^-_j=w|_{I_j}(x_j)$ for the trace from the left cell and $w^+_j=w|_{I_{j+1}}(x_j)$ for the trace from the right cell; the chosen face normal points from left to right, and the jump is $[w]_j=w^+_j-w^-_j$. At $a$ and $b$, the outward normals are $-1$ and $+1$, respectively.

The published matching-affine-simplicial-mesh convention used elsewhere on the A page has dimension $d\ge2$. This definition supplies the distinct one-dimensional interval and trace convention; it makes no assertion about multidimensional cells.
items.strategy: The published simplicial-mesh definition is explicitly for dimension at least two; supply the separate one-dimensional convention needed by the transport and SBP cases.

items.title: Diagonal-norm summation-by-parts element data
items.statement:
On an affine element in dimension $d\ge1$, diagonal-norm SBP data consist of a nodal state vector with $N_K$ entries, a positive diagonal matrix $H_K\in\mathbb R^{N_K\times N_K}$, and derivative matrices $D_{K,\ell}$, $1\le\ell\le d$. Put $Q_{K,\ell}=H_KD_{K,\ell}$. For each face $F$ let $R_{K,F}$ select its face nodes from the volume nodes, let $M_{K,F}$ be a positive diagonal face quadrature matrix, and let $n_{K,F}$ be its constant outward unit normal. The data are **SBP compatible** when
$$D_{K,\ell}\mathbf1=0,\qquad R_{K,F}\mathbf1=\mathbf1_F,\qquad Q_{K,\ell}+Q_{K,\ell}^{T}=\sum_{F\subset\partial K} n_{K,F,\ell}R_{K,F}^{T}M_{K,F}R_{K,F}$$
for each coordinate $\ell$. The rows of $R_{K,F}$ select the nodes used by the face quadrature; on an interior face, the two cells have the same face nodes and weights under the face identification and opposite normals. In dimension one, $R_L$ and $R_R$ select the left and right endpoint nodes with normals $-1$ and $+1$.

This is conditional algebraic data: the definition does not assert that every mesh has such a rule. The identities include exact affine metric factors and no curved-element metric approximation.
items.strategy: Make all matrix sizes, orientations, positivity requirements and exact identities part of the data; assert no existence for arbitrary meshes.

items.title: Forward-Euler step for degree-zero upwind DG transport
items.statement:
Input a dimension $d\ge2$, a finite matching affine simplicial mesh $\mathcal T_h$ whose boundary faces are paired by translations to form a periodic mesh, a constant velocity $\beta\in\mathbb R^d$, one cell mean $U_K\in\mathbb R$ per cell, and a step $\Delta t>0$. The output is either `CFL-inadmissible` or an updated vector of cell means $U^+=(U_K^+)_{K\in\mathcal T_h}$. Let $V_K=\int_K1\,dx$ be the cell volume and $A_F=\int_F1\,dS$ the face area. For each face $F\subset\partial K$, let $n_{K,F}$ be the outward unit normal, $b_{K,F}=\beta\cdot n_{K,F}$, and $K_F$ the neighboring cell across that periodic face. With $b^+=\max(b,0)$ and $b^- =\min(b,0)$, the upwind flux out of $K$ is
$$\widehat f_{K,F}=b_{K,F}^+U_K+b_{K,F}^-U_{K_F}.$$

Compute
$$\lambda_K=\frac{\Delta t}{V_K}\sum_{F\subset\partial K}A_Fb_{K,F}^+.$$
If $\lambda_K>1$ for any cell, return `CFL-inadmissible` without updating the state. Otherwise, the **degree-zero upwind forward-Euler update** is admissible and its output is
$$U_K^+=U_K-\frac{\Delta t}{V_K}\sum_{F\subset\partial K}A_F\widehat f_{K,F}.$$
This is the degree-zero specialization of [[def-pe04-upwind-dg-transport-discretization]].
items.strategy: Give the exact volume-weighted coefficient form of the one-step cell update; make periodic indexing explicit.

items.title: Cellwise L2 projection relation onto broken polynomials
items.statement:
Let $K$ be a cell in the one-dimensional interval or $d\ge2$ matching affine-simplex branch of [[def-pe04-upwind-dg-transport-discretization]], and fix an integer degree $p\ge0$. Let $(K,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a finite measure space as in [[def-measure-space]], let $\mathcal L^2(\mu)$ have the raw measurable-function meaning of [[def-calligraphic-l-p-on-a-measure-space]], and let $W=\mathbb P_p(K)\subseteq\mathcal L^2(\mu)$. For $u\in\mathcal L^2(\mu)$ define its **cellwise L2 projection relation** to be the set
$$\mathcal P_K(u)=\left\{p\in\mathbb P_p(K):\int_K(u-p)w\,d\mu=0\text{ for every }w\in\mathbb P_p(K)\right\}.$$
For a mesh, the broken relation is the product of these cell relations. The measure $\mu$ is required to give positive measure to every nonempty relatively open subset of $K$ when existence and uniqueness are claimed. This definition does not itself assert that the set is a singleton. Whenever a later result proves that the relation has a unique member, write $\Pi_Ku$ for that member.
items.strategy: State the inner-product equations without assuming existence or uniqueness; prove both before using the projection operator.

items.title: Upwind SBP-SAT discretization of constant transport
items.statement:
Fix constant transport velocity $\beta\in\mathbb R^d$ and SBP data from [[def-pe04-diagonal-norm-sbp-element-data]]. For each cell $K$, let $U_K(t)$ be the vector of nodal values, $Q_{K,\ell}=H_KD_{K,\ell}$, and $U_{K,F}=R_{K,F}U_K$. Set $b_{K,F}=\beta\cdot n_{K,F}$. At each interior face, use the trace from the cell with positive outward speed when $b_{K,F}>0$, and the neighboring trace when $b_{K,F}<0$; at boundary faces use the inflow data on $b_{K,F}<0$ and the interior trace on $b_{K,F}\ge0$. Denote this upwind scalar trace by $\widehat U_{K,F}$.

The **upwind SBP-SAT semidiscretization** is
$$H_K\dot U_K+\sum_{\ell=1}^d\beta_\ell Q_{K,\ell}U_K+\sum_{F\subset\partial K}R_{K,F}^{T}M_{K,F}\,b_{K,F}(\widehat U_{K,F}-U_{K,F})=0.$$
The sign of the SAT correction is fixed by this equation. The definition is spatial only and makes no fully discrete claim.
items.strategy: State the exact SAT sign and use the same oriented upwind flux as the DG definition.

items.title: Upwind DG transport satisfies the semidiscrete L2 energy identity
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$. If $d=1$, let $\mathcal T_h$ be a finite oriented interval mesh of $\Omega=(a,b)$, $a<b$, from [[def-pe04-one-dimensional-interval-mesh-and-broken-polynomials]]; if $d\ge2$, let $\mathcal T_h$ be a finite matching affine simplicial mesh of $\Omega$. Let $\beta\in\mathbb R^d$ be constant, and let $u_h$ solve [[def-pe04-upwind-dg-transport-discretization]] with inflow data $g$. Assume Countable Choice when $d\ge2$, as required by the affine-simplex Green supplier; no choice assumption is needed for the interval branch. Write $\Gamma_+=\{x\in\partial\Omega:\beta\cdot n>0\}$ and $\Gamma_- =\{x\in\partial\Omega:\beta\cdot n<0\}$. For an interior facet $F=K^-\cap K^+$ choose a unit normal $n_F$ from $K^-$ to $K^+$ and write $[u_h]=u_h^+-u_h^-$. In dimension one, integrals over facets and boundary points mean sums with respect to zero-dimensional surface measure. Then
$$\frac12\frac{d}{dt}\sum_{K\in\mathcal T_h}\|u_h\|_{L^2(K)}^2+\frac12\sum_{F\text{ interior}}\int_F|\beta\cdot n_F|[u_h]^2\,dS+\frac12\int_{\Gamma_+}(\beta\cdot n)u_h^2\,dS+\frac12\int_{\Gamma_-}|\beta\cdot n|(u_h-g)^2\,dS=\frac12\int_{\Gamma_-}|\beta\cdot n|g^2\,dS.$$
The equality is understood in $\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$. It is a finite energy balance whenever $\int_{\Gamma_-}|\beta\cdot n|g^2\,dS<\infty$ at the time in question; otherwise both sides are $+\infty$ and give no finite inflow bound. In particular, zero inflow data give a nonincreasing semidiscrete $L^2$ norm. This result is semidiscrete and makes no claim about a time integrator.
items.strategy: Use the actual simplex Green identity and opposite interior normals, then calculate each signed upwind face contribution.

items.title: Conservative flux-differencing SBP method for nonlinear systems
items.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let $\mathcal T_h$ be a finite matching affine simplicial mesh, and consider $U_t+\sum_{\ell=1}^d\partial_{x_\ell}F_\ell(U)=0$ with state domain $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathbb R^m$. Assume a common convex entropy $\eta$ and, for each direction $\ell$, an entropy flux $q_\ell$ so that $(\eta,q_\ell)$ satisfies [[def-pe03-system-entropy-pair-and-potential]] for the directional flux $F_\ell$. Write $v=\nabla\eta$ and $\psi_\ell=v^TF_\ell-q_\ell$. For every direction, supply a symmetric consistent two-point flux $F_\ell^{ec}$ satisfying [[def-pe03-tadmor-entropy-conservative-flux]], namely
$$\bigl(v(U_R)-v(U_L)\bigr)^TF_\ell^{ec}(U_L,U_R)=\psi_\ell(U_R)-\psi_\ell(U_L).$$

On each cell use diagonal-norm SBP data from [[def-pe04-diagonal-norm-sbp-element-data]]. Put $Q_{K,\ell}=H_KD_{K,\ell}$; let $U_i^K\in\mathcal A$ be the nodal states; and let the face restrictions select paired face nodes with matching positive weights on the two incident cells. For an oriented interior face node with normal $n$ from the minus trace to the plus trace, set $F_n(U)=\sum_\ell n_\ell F_\ell(U)$ and $\psi_n(U)=\sum_\ell n_\ell\psi_\ell(U)$. Given any fixed coefficient $\alpha_{F,q}\ge0$, define the normal interface flux
$$\widehat F_{n,F,q}^*(U^-,U^+)=\sum_{\ell=1}^d n_\ell F_\ell^{ec}(U^-,U^+)-\frac{\alpha_{F,q}}2\bigl(v(U^+)-v(U^-)\bigr).$$
The coefficient is the same when the face orientation is reversed. Thus the flux is conservative and consistent, and its entropy contraction is
$$[v]^T\widehat F_{n,F,q}^*=[\psi_n]-\frac{\alpha_{F,q}}2\lVert[v]\rVert^2\le[\psi_n],$$
by the directional Tadmor identities in [[def-pe03-tadmor-entropy-conservative-flux]]. On physical boundary faces supply a consistent normal flux and require the boundary entropy contribution below to be nonnegative.

Write $\omega_{F,q}$ for the $q$th diagonal entry of $M_F$. Define the boundary entropy contribution
$$\mathcal B_h(t)=\sum_{F\subset\partial\Omega}\sum_q\omega_{F,q}\bigl(v(U_{F,q})^T\widehat F_{n_F}^*-\psi_{n_F}(U_{F,q})\bigr).$$
The selected boundary flux is entropy admissible when $\mathcal B_h(t)\ge0$. The **flux-differencing SBP semidiscretization** on each element is
$$H_K\dot U^K+2\sum_{\ell=1}^d\bigl(Q_{K,\ell}\circ F_\ell^{ec}(U^K,U^K)\bigr)\mathbf1+\sum_{F\subset\partial K}R_{K,F}^TM_{K,F}\bigl(\widehat F_{n_{K,F}}^*-F_{n_{K,F}}(U_{K,F})\bigr)=0,$$
where $\circ$ is entrywise matrix multiplication and $F_\ell^{ec}(U^K,U^K)$ is the matrix with $(i,j)$ entry $F_\ell^{ec}(U_i^K,U_j^K)$. These are conditional method data: compatible SBP data and directional entropy-conservative fluxes are hypotheses, not asserted to exist for every mesh or entropy pair. The interior numerical flux is explicitly defined once those data and $\alpha_{F,q}$ are supplied. Curved elements are excluded.
items.strategy: State the entropy-pair and flux assumptions direction by direction, the exact SBP/metric identities, paired nodes, face SAT and boundary entropy condition; exclude curved meshes.

items.title: The cellwise L2 projection exists uniquely and is best approximation
items.statement:
For every finite measure $\mu$ on a bounded nondegenerate interval or nondegenerate affine simplex $K$ that assigns positive measure to every nonempty relatively open subset, every integer degree $p\ge0$ with $\mathbb P_p(K)\subseteq\mathcal L^2(\mu)$ as in [[def-pe04-cellwise-l2-projection]], and every $u\in\mathcal L^2(\mu)$, the set $\mathcal P_K(u)$ contains exactly one polynomial $\Pi_Ku$. For each $w\in\mathbb P_p(K)$,
$$\|u-\Pi_Ku\|_{L^2(K)}\le\|u-w\|_{L^2(K)}.$$
items.strategy: Use positive definiteness of the finite-dimensional Gram matrix and the Pythagorean identity.

items.title: The degree-zero upwind forward-Euler step preserves mass and convex entropy
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal T_h$ be a finite periodic matching affine simplicial mesh in $d\ge2$, let $\beta\in\mathbb R^d$ be constant, and apply [[alg-pe04-first-order-upwind-forward-euler]] with $\lambda_K\le1$ for every cell. Assume Countable Choice for the imported affine-simplex Green formula. Then the cell-volume-weighted mean is conserved:
$$\sum_KV_KU_K^+=\sum_KV_KU_K.$$
For every convex function $\eta:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, the weighted discrete entropy does not increase:
$$\sum_KV_K\eta(U_K^+)\le\sum_KV_K\eta(U_K).$$
items.strategy: Rewrite each cell update as a convex combination using the zero total normal flux identity, apply Jensen, and reindex paired face contributions.

items.title: Upwind SBP-SAT transport satisfies the semidiscrete L2 energy identity
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$. If $d=1$, let the cells be a finite oriented interval mesh from [[def-pe04-one-dimensional-interval-mesh-and-broken-polynomials]]; if $d\ge2$, let them form a finite matching affine simplicial mesh. On every cell assume diagonal-norm SBP data of [[def-pe04-diagonal-norm-sbp-element-data]], with paired interior face nodes, equal paired weights, and opposite outward normals. Let $\beta\in\mathbb R^d$ be constant, and let the differentiable nodal state $U_K(t)$ solve the upwind SBP-SAT method of [[def-pe04-upwind-sbp-sat-transport-discretization]] with prescribed inflow values $g_{F,q}$ where $b_{K,F}:=\beta\cdot n_{K,F}<0$. Write $\omega_{F,q}$ for the diagonal entries of the face norm. On an interior face oriented from $K^-$ to $K^+$, set $b_F=\beta\cdot n_F$ and $[U]_{F,q}=U^+_{F,q}-U^-_{F,q}$. Let $\Gamma_+$ and $\Gamma_-$ denote the boundary faces with positive and negative outward speed, respectively. For $d=1$, each face has one endpoint node and its face sum is a one-point sum. The discrete energy $E_h=\frac12\sum_K U_K^TH_KU_K$ satisfies
$$\frac{dE_h}{dt}+\frac12\sum_{F\text{ interior}}\sum_q\omega_{F,q}|b_F|[U]_{F,q}^2+\frac12\sum_{F\subset\Gamma_+}\sum_q\omega_{F,q}b_{K,F}U_{F,q}^2+\frac12\sum_{F\subset\Gamma_-}\sum_q\omega_{F,q}|b_{K,F}|(U_{F,q}-g_{F,q})^2=\frac12\sum_{F\subset\Gamma_-}\sum_q\omega_{F,q}|b_{K,F}|g_{F,q}^2.$$
Consequently, zero inflow data give a nonincreasing SBP norm.
items.strategy: Contract the matrix ODE with the state, apply the stated SBP identity, and pair the two traces at each interface.

items.title: Smooth-solution L2 error bound for upwind DG transport
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$. If $d=1$, let $\Omega=(a,b)$, $a<b$, have a finite oriented interval mesh $\mathcal T_h$ from [[def-pe04-one-dimensional-interval-mesh-and-broken-polynomials]]; if $d\ge2$, let $\mathcal T_h$ be a finite matching affine simplicial mesh of $\Omega$. Let $\beta\in\mathbb R^d$ be constant, and let $u\in C^1([0,T]\times\overline\Omega)$ solve $u_t+\beta\cdot\nabla u=0$ with inflow data equal to its boundary trace. Assume Countable Choice for the imported affine-simplex Green and Lebesgue-measure suppliers; the full-support and finite-measure properties on each cell are established below. Let $u_h$ be the semidiscrete upwind DG solution of degree $p\ge0$, and let $\Pi_h$ be the cellwise L2 projection with respect to Lebesgue measure on each cell. Use $\|w\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2=\sum_K\int_K|w|^2\,dx$ and put $\eta=\Pi_hu-u$. For an interior face with chosen normal $n_F$, let $\eta^{\mathrm{up}}$ be the trace of $\eta$ from the upwind side. In dimension one, face and boundary integrals are sums with respect to zero-dimensional surface measure. Define
$$R_h(t)^2=\sum_{F\text{ interior}}\int_F|\beta\cdot n_F|\,|\eta^{\mathrm{up}}|^2\,dS+\int_{\Gamma_+}(\beta\cdot n)|\eta|^2\,dS.$$
Then
$$\|u_h(T)-u(T)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le\left(\|u_h(0)-\Pi_hu(0)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2+2\int_0^TR_h(t)^2\,dt\right)^{1/2}+\|\Pi_hu(T)-u(T)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.$$
This is an exact projection-trace residual bound. It asserts no mesh-order rate unless the displayed projection errors are separately estimated.
items.strategy: Subtract the exact weak equation, use cellwise projection orthogonality to cancel volume residuals, and absorb face residuals with upwind dissipation.

items.title: Flux-differencing SBP is conservative and semidiscretely entropy stable
items.statement:
Assume the affine-element method and all directional entropy/SBP data of [[def-pe04-flux-differencing-sbp-systems]]. Suppose all nodal states remain in $\mathcal A$. Define the discrete entropy and the boundary contribution by
$$E_h(t)=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T_h}\mathbf1^TH_K\eta(U^K),\qquad \mathcal B_h(t)=\sum_{F\subset\partial\Omega}\sum_q\omega_{F,q}\bigl(v(U_{F,q})^T\widehat F_{n_F}^*-\psi_{n_F}(U_{F,q})\bigr).$$
If $\mathcal B_h(t)\ge0$, then
$$\frac{d}{dt}E_h(t)+\sum_{F\text{ interior}}\sum_q\omega_{F,q}\frac{\alpha_{F,q}}2\lVert[v]_{F,q}\rVert^2+\mathcal B_h(t)=0,$$
so $E_h$ is nonincreasing. Here $\widehat F_{n_F,q}^*$ is the explicitly defined normal flux of [[def-pe04-flux-differencing-sbp-systems]], and the boundary sum is over physical boundary faces. For the periodic conclusion, assume each identified boundary-face pair has matching nodes and positive weights and opposite normals. Treat each pair as one interior face using the flux above on the paired traces, with the same $\alpha_{F,q}$ under orientation reversal; include it in the interior-face dissipation sum and omit it from $\mathcal B_h$. The conservative state-flux contributions of each pair cancel, while its entropy contribution is the same nonnegative interface dissipation in the displayed identity. The same semidiscretization conserves the quadrature-weighted total state on such a periodic mesh. No fully discrete entropy statement follows.
items.strategy: Use symmetry and directional Tadmor identities in the volume pair sum, convert to face terms with SBP, cancel conservative state fluxes and retain entropy jump dissipation on ordinary and periodic interfaces.

items.title: SSPRK(3,3) preserves the degree-zero upwind entropy bound
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal T_h$ be a finite periodic matching affine simplicial mesh, write $V_K=\int_K1\,dx>0$ for its cell volumes, let $\beta$ be constant, and let $\eta:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be convex. Assume the cellwise forward-Euler condition in [[thm-pe04-first-order-upwind-forward-euler-conservation-and-entropy]] holds for $\Delta t$, including its Countable Choice premise through the affine-simplex Green formula. For the autonomous degree-zero upwind DG ODE, write $E_{\Delta t}(U)=U+\Delta t L_h(U)$. The exact SSPRK(3,3) recurrence is
$$Y_1=E_{\Delta t}(U^n),\qquad Y_2=\frac34U^n+\frac14E_{\Delta t}(Y_1),\qquad U^{n+1}=\frac13U^n+\frac23E_{\Delta t}(Y_2).$$
Then $\sum_KV_K\eta(U_K^{n+1})\le\sum_KV_K\eta(U_K^n)$. This guarantee is for the degree-zero scalar upwind operator just specified; it is not a fully discrete entropy theorem for the high-order nonlinear flux-differencing SBP method.
items.strategy: Instantiate NA15's coefficient-one convex transfer with the weighted scalar entropy; assert no transfer to the high-order nonlinear DG/SBP semidiscretization.

title: Hyperbolic DG and summation-by-parts methods — Examples

items.title: Underintegrated Burgers collocation can increase quadratic entropy
items.statement: The SBP matrix identity alone guarantees that a naively collocated strong-form discretization of a nonlinear conservation law cannot increase its discrete quadratic entropy.
items.strategy: Verify the SBP matrix identity and compute the exact nodal residual and weighted entropy derivative.

items.title: Central and upwind fluxes have different periodic dissipation
items.statement: On two equal periodic interval cells of length $h$, consider degree-zero DG for $u_t+a u_x=0$ with $a>0$ and cell states $u_1,u_2$. Compare the central flux $\widehat f_c(a_0,b_0)=a(a_0+b_0)/2$ with the upwind flux $\widehat f_u(a_0,b_0)=a a_0$.

items.title: A constant upwind DG state with inflow data on one interval
items.statement: Take the one-cell interval $K=(0,1)$, degree $p=0$, speed $a>0$, constant cell state $U(t)$, and inflow value $g(t)$ at $x=0$. The outflow trace at $x=1$ is $U(t)$.
items.strategy: Evaluate the three oriented face fluxes and simplify the scalar energy identity.

items.title: The SBP inflow SAT produces the boundary energy term
items.statement:
On the interval $[0,1]$, use two endpoint nodes, $H=\frac12I$, $D=\begin{pmatrix}-1&1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}$, left and right selectors $R_L=(1,0)$ and $R_R=(0,1)$, and $B=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1)$. For $u_t+a u_x=0$ with $a>0$, inflow value $g(t)$ at $x=0$, and upwind outflow at $x=1$, the SBP-SAT ODE is
$$H\dot U+aHD\,U+a e_L(U_L-g)=0.$$
items.strategy: Insert the explicit H, D and boundary vectors, then contract the exact SAT equation with the nodal state.
